capabilities.note: `forge tree [--sprint <id>] [--json]` and `forge sprint inspect <id> [--json]` are additional local projections of this same query (ADR 0005) — not separate capabilities, and not covered by the automated CLI-surface parity check below. The Desktop dashboard's sprint tree and sprint detail views are their counterpart and render the same shared lines.

`forge sprint inspect` shares the `sprint` command group but belongs to project.snapshot (a query), not this mutation capability. `forge sprint rebase` is a separate capability (`sprint.rebase`) below, not one of this id's verbs. `--title` (ADR 0057) applies to the `create` verb only; it is written after the verb alternatives so the documented-CLI parity check still reads them as sibling subcommands.

Not implemented on either surface. `SprintGitIsolation.RebaseAttemptAsync` (the git-level primitive this would wrap) already exists but has no reachable trigger: it recovers from a concurrent-integration race that can only occur once a node executor drives attempts through `SprintGitIsolation.IntegrateAsync`, and no executor exists yet (ADR 0020, ADR 0027).

Confirms a `NodeRole.Confirmation` node's own attempt lifecycle (no executor exists for this role -- `ExecutionProfilePolicy.PhaseFor` returns null for it) rather than through a human gate. Desktop parity (ADR 0037) reuses `MainPageViewModel.ResolveGateAsync`'s blank-means-active-sprint/ambiguity resolution and mandatory-confirmation shape exactly.

Settles a `NodeRole.TestWork` node's own attempt lifecycle (no executor exists for this role either -- `ExecutionProfilePolicy.PhaseFor` returns null for it too) rather than through a human gate. Unlike `workflow.confirm`, no downstream eligibility gate reads the recorded artifact's content -- `review`'s own graph dependency on this node is satisfied by the node reaching `succeeded` alone. Desktop parity landed alongside `workflow.confirm`/`workflow.finalize` (ADR 0037).

Merges the sprint's isolated integration branch into the project's own default branch (frozen as `SprintDefinition.DefaultBranch` at sprint creation) and completes the sprint -- fast-forward-only, refusing on a dirty or wrong-branch working directory, never running `git checkout` itself (ADR 0036). This is the first Forge operation of any kind that mutates the project's own working directory rather than an isolated worktree, so it stays human-only with no config-driven confirmation bypass, matching `workflow.review`/`attempt.supersede`/`workflow.confirm`/`workflow.test_work`. Desktop parity landed in ADR 0037.

Implemented on Host and CLI (plan section 6.2, Slice 4, ADR 0049); Desktop parity is deferred to a later slice, matching ADR 0037's CLI-first precedent. The Host answers only for its own project (ADR 0005); the CLI's `forge workspace summary` fans out across every `forge project`-cataloged root itself. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- that list requires both surfaces (capabilities.json's own `public_requires_both_surfaces` rule).

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 6.3, Slice 4/ADR 0049; Desktop's SprintWorkspace/Timeline, Slice 6/ADR 0051). Projects the existing append-only workflow journal -- user messages (`sprint.post_message` below) are now their own event type in this same journal, and agent summaries are projected from the existing `Handoff.Summary` a node already records (ADR 0054 closes the gap ADR 0049 originally deferred). Redacted twice: once when the projector builds each item, again at render time. ADR 0059 adds an optional structured `payload` to each item (page contract `1.2.0`, `event.schema.json` `1.1.0`): an `AttemptDiffRecorded` item carries `payload.diff` with the attempt's per-file git statistics, capped at 50 files with the remainder counted in `elided_files`. Diff hunk content is never persisted. Both redaction passes cover the payload. ADR 0060 adds a second payload family (page contract `1.3.0`, `event.schema.json` `1.2.0`): an `AttemptToolUseRecorded` item carries `payload.tool_use` with what that attempt's provider actually did -- per-call kind (`command`/`edit`), Forge-observed duration, a command's exit code and success, and an edit's worktree-relative path -- capped at 50 calls with the remainder counted in `elided_calls`, plus an `unmapped_items` drift count. Command text and command output are never persisted. Recorded only for a provider whose adapter extracts tool calls (Codex today; Claude is deferred). Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- ADR 0051 keeps this reserved, matching ADR 0047/0048/0049/0050's own precedent, since promoting it also requires widening `SurfaceParityTests.DesktopControls`'s fixed dictionary, a separable follow-up.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 6.4, Slice 4/ADR 0049; Desktop's SprintWorkspace/ContextualActions, Slice 6/ADR 0051). Wraps already-existing computations rather than a parallel policy engine: the project-level suggested-action list (`StatusAdvisor.Recommend`) without a sprint, and `StageTransitionAssessor`'s own assessment per candidate stage plus sprint-lifecycle state for a given sprint. ADR 0058 adds a node-scoped `approve_gate:<node-id>`/`reject_gate:<node-id>` pair per pending human gate, each executed through `workflow.review` above and each carrying `target.timeline_sequence` -- the sequence of the exact journal event that requested the decision. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- ADR 0051 keeps this reserved for the same reason as `sprint.timeline`.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 7, Slice 2/ADR 0044/0047; Desktop's SprintWorkspace/StopOperation, Slice 6/ADR 0051). The Desktop control re-validates the exact stoppable operation immediately before showing its confirmation, which names the target node/attempt. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- that list requires both surfaces (capabilities.json's own `public_requires_both_surfaces` rule); ADR 0051 keeps it reserved as a separable cleanup, matching ADR 0047/0048/0049/0050's own precedent.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 8.1, Slice 3/ADR 0045/0046/0048; Desktop's SprintWorkspace/AssessStageTransition, Slice 6/ADR 0051). Read-only by design -- the UI may render this projection but never calculates or overrides it; Desktop re-fetches a fresh assessment immediately before every confirmation and commit rather than trusting an earlier render. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- ADR 0051 keeps this reserved for the same reason as `workflow.stop_operation`.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 8.5, Slice 3/ADR 0045/0046/0048; Desktop's SprintWorkspace/MoveStage, Slice 6/ADR 0051). The Host recomputes the assessment immediately before mutation; a rewind always requires a bounded reason and mandatory confirmation (plan section 8.4), which Desktop's own dialog collects and forwards verbatim, never a hardcoded value. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented` -- ADR 0051 keeps this reserved for the same reason as `workflow.stop_operation`.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 6.5, Slice 7, ADR 0043/0052). Distinct from `provider.health`: reports verified account/model quota, never sprint retry budget. ADR 0052's investigation found no provider integration in this codebase (Claude Code, Codex) exposes a verified quota signal, so every reading currently projects `unknown`, truthfully -- see ADR 0052. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented`, matching ADR 0049/0050/0051's own precedent for `workspace.summary`/`sprint.timeline`/`workspace.available_actions`: promoting it is a separable follow-up (widening `SurfaceParityTests.DesktopControls`'s fixed dictionary) that does not gate this capability's own functional correctness, since Desktop already consumes it through the same local, in-process call every other reserved read model uses.

Implemented on Host, CLI, and Desktop (plan section 4.3/6.3, post-release timeline gap closure, ADR 0054). Appends a `UserMessagePosted` WorkflowEvent to the sprint's existing append-only journal rather than a second store, so it gets the same dense per-sprint Sequence, redaction, and restart-persistence machinery every other timeline item already has (`sprint.timeline`'s own note above is updated by the same ADR: agent summaries are now also projected, from the existing `Handoff.Summary` a node already records). Not confirmable -- posting a message is additive, not destructive. Not yet in `CapabilityIds.Implemented`, matching ADR 0049/0050/0051's own precedent for `sprint.timeline`/`workflow.stop_operation`/`sprint.move_stage`: promoting it is a separable follow-up that also requires widening `SurfaceParityTests.DesktopCapabilityCalls`'s fixed dictionary.
